_README: Reviewed readers of the work-identity columns (job_title, responsibilities). Each entry is a
live function ("function") or view ("view") a reviewer read and confirmed is NOT a permission
decision. purpose is one of display | write | search | invite-copy. Each entry is PINNED to the
definition that was read: defined_in is the migration of its last definition and fingerprint
the guard's hash of that definition (comments stripped, whitespace normalised). A changed body
or a later redefinition fails the guard (R4) until someone re-reads it and re-pins it. The list
only shrinks: an entry that stops matching a live reader fails (R4). A policy (R1) or an
authorization-helper-shaped function or view (R2) that reads a title can never be listed here.
non_identity_columns pins every live column of the two tables that carry a work identity that is
NOT work identity. A column added to either table under any name fails (R6) until it is
classified in the same PR: into WORK_IDENTITY_BY_TABLE in the guard if it describes what a person
does or is called, otherwise into this list. A pinned column that is no longer live fails (R4).
retired_role_sql / retired_role_ts (R7) name the only places allowed to name the retired title role
"coach" beside a role word: code that reads the value only to refuse it or to remove it, and code a
reviewer confirmed uses it as data, not as a role (an assignment seat label). Each is pinned to the body
a reviewer read (sql: defined_in + fingerprint; ts: path + fingerprint of the statement). A changed body
fails (R4) until re-read; an entry that stops matching fails (R4), so the lists only shrink.

sql.reason: Copies the accepted invitation's title and responsibilities onto the new membership; the membership's role comes from default_role, never from the title. Re-read for EXP08 owners 20271117170008: an owner invitation now seats an owner only after re-checking that the sender is still the account holder (is_tenant_account_holder) and that the legal owner's seat is open; the title is still only copied. Re-read again for round 2 (2026-10-27): the record's updated_by is no longer stamped with the invitee; the title is still only copied. Re-read for round 3 (2026-10-27): the tenant row and the sender's seat are locked FOR SHARE before the sender check; the title is still only copied.

sql.function: public.create_solo_team_invite(uuid, uuid, text, text, text, text, boolean, uuid, jsonb)
sql.reason: Stores the invited person's title and responsibilities (and, since EXP08, the Team conversations choice) on the invitation row after solo_team_invite_authority() authorizes the actor; the access granted is _permission, checked against owner | admin | member, and Owner additionally requires the account holder (_assert_tenant_account_holder, EXP08 owners 20271117170008). The title never enters either check.

Hands PAIGE the roster's and pending invitations' work identity as context; what the caller may see is decided by role and is_owner, and the payload declares custom_work_identity_changes_authority = false.
Returns each member's title and responsibilities for the Team roster and matches the owner's search text against them (ILIKE); roster access is decided first, from role and is_owner.

Carries the old invitation's title and responsibilities into its replacement through create_solo_team_invite; authority is resolved by solo_team_invite_authority(), and for an owner invitation by _assert_tenant_account_holder (EXP08 owners 20271117170008). Re-read for round 3 (2026-10-27): an owner invitation whose legal owner was deleted (business_owner_removed_at) is refused before anything is copied; the title is still only copied.
Writes the two columns only after is_tenant_admin() authorizes the caller, then echoes the saved values back; nothing branches on them.

Returns each active teammate's title in the Team Hub roster so namesakes can be told apart in the @ picker; who may see the roster is the caller's active seat in a canonical SOLO workspace, and permission is derived from role and is_owner, never the title. Re-read for EXP08 Team Hub agents A1a: the re-emit adds agent_key, agent_name_clash (from the display name, not the title) and counts an agent's row as unread; the title is still only echoed for display.

retired_role_sql.reason: Refuses an invitation that carries the retired role before any role is written. Re-read and re-pinned for 20271110040000, which only schema-qualifies digest() as extensions.digest(); the refusal is unchanged.

Refuses a change to the retired role by name before any write. First judged when 20271115030008 re-emitted it (admin scope stage 0 changed who may call it and requires the target to be an active member of the workspace); the coach refusal is the body production already ran.

Refuses a grant of the retired role by name before any write. Re-read and re-pinned for 20271115030008, which stops the global 'admin' user_roles insert and writes any other global role only for a person already active in the workspace (or on an operator path), and refuses a row-listed operator-tier role up front with PROTECTED_ROLE_GRANT_FORBIDDEN; the coach refusal is unchanged and still first.
Refuses a revoke of the retired role by name before any write, so the seat resync never runs for a value no row can hold.

retired_role_ts.reason: The assignment SEAT label passed to assign_contact (p_role), a data value naming which seat an assignment fills; it grants nothing and reads no role.
A refusal: the set of role-name literals that may never be used as an owner-grantable capability permission.
A refusal: RETIRED_ROLES lists the values an invitation may not carry; the invitation is refused before any role is written.
